title: Donut Advanced Labels — Swatch + Value Block Rendering

complexity.rationale: Scope narrowed to the swatch+text block's rendering and positioning (connector-line generation is now its own spec, donut-advanced-labels-connector-line, and collision avoidance reuses donut-direct-labels-collision rather than being reimplemented here). A swatch rendered as its own mark inside a donut label has no existing precedent in this codebase, and extending the direct-label hemisphere anchor technique from two text lines to a 4-part block is real new logic - but the value/detail row rendering and data reuse (the existing `_sumData` aggregate) are straightforward. The real-text-measurement question inherited from donut-direct-labels still applies here too, at a larger (4-part) block.

summary: Advanced labels are a not-yet-built Donut child component: a label block (color swatch + segment name on one row, value/percent below, an optional exact-value detail row below that), positioned around the ring the same way direct labels are. Confirmed against a live Figma example showing all three documented elements (swatch+name, bold value/%, and a 'X out of Y' detail row). The connector leader line connecting each label to its slice is tracked separately in donut-advanced-labels-connector-line; collision avoidance when labels stack is handled by donut-direct-labels-collision, reused rather than reimplemented.
requirements: Render a swatch (fixed 16px, using the existing roundedSquarePath SVG shape - reuse it, don't invent a new shape) + segment name on the same row (never stacked), gap 8px between them (`chart.donut.spacing.advanced-label-swatch-gap`).

Below that row: the value and/or percent, in `text-primary` (gray-800) - confirmed against the Figma example ('60.8%', '32.4%', '6.8%' all render in the darker gray-800, not the gray-700 used by direct labels' value text). Gap between the name row and the value/% row is 4px (`chart.donut.spacing.advanced-label-name-value-gap`).

Below the value/%, an optional detail row in the format '{segment value} out of {total value}' (confirmed via the Figma example: '440 out of 6,458', '2,092 out of 6,458', '3,926 out of 6,458', where 6,458 is the same aggregated total the DonutSummary/metric-total already computes), rendered in `text-secondary` (gray-700). Gap between the value/% row and the detail row is 0px (`chart.donut.spacing.advanced-label-value-detail-gap`) - directly adjacent.

The value/% row and the detail row are left-aligned to the swatch's left edge, not to the name (which starts to the right of the swatch, after the 8px gap) - confirmed visually (both rows start at the same x as the swatch, not indented under the name text).

Swatch is always the leftmost element of the label block on both hemispheres - the 'swatch -> name -> value/% -> detail' reading order never flips. The hemisphere-mirrored anchor-shift technique from donut-direct-labels (move the anchor point per hemisphere, don't flip the alignment property) extends to the whole swatch+text block here, not just text lines - confirmed in the Figma example (swatch is the leftmost element for North America, EMEA, and Others alike, regardless of hemisphere).

Gap from the ring is 20px (`chart.donut.spacing.label-ring-gap`, shared with direct labels), measured against the whole block's real rendered bounding box (swatch + all text rows together), not an anchor coordinate - the label must never overlap the ring.

edgeCases.case: Very long segment name, or a detail row whose numbers are unusually wide
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The 20px ring gap is measured against the whole block's real rendered bounding box; confirm whether the block wraps, truncates, or simply grows outward when its widest row exceeds the space available before the chart edge.

edgeCases.case: Many small adjacent segments clustered in the same hemisphere
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Reuses donut-direct-labels-collision's cascade + horizontal re-anchor, with this feature's own ~58px minGap (taller 3-row block) rather than direct labels' two-line height - not a separately reimplemented algorithm.

edgeCases.case: Direct labels and advanced labels combined on the same chart
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Per donut-advanced-labels, combining is supported ('to emphasize a state') - confirm the shared collision util (donut-direct-labels-collision) handles both label types' blocks correctly when both are stacked in the same hemisphere.

edgeCases.case: detail row omitted (value/% only, no 'X out of Y' row)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Block height for collision purposes (minGap) shrinks accordingly since the detail row is optional per the skill.

Direct labels (SegmentLabel) are already unsupported for boolean donuts - confirm whether advanced labels should follow the same restriction, given the 'X out of Y' detail row's total-value concept may not translate cleanly to a boolean/percent-only donut.

Per donut-chart-tokens' behavior tokens, the hovered segment's advanced-label value/% switches to that segment's own categorical color, and non-hovered labels fade - the same mechanism proposed in the donut-hover spec should extend to this new mark rather than being reimplemented separately.

crossCutting.notes: touchesHoverAnimation/touchesControlledHighlight: donut-chart-tokens' behavior tokens explicitly document the same hover value-color-switch and fade behavior for advanced labels as for direct labels (see the donut-hover spec) - this should share that mechanism, not reimplement it, and inherits the same open question about whether controlled-highlight (not just mouse hover) should also drive it. touchesTooltipOrPopover: true because (a) this is a brand-new interactive-adjacent mark that needs its own tooltip for chartPopovers/chartInspects wiring decisions, and (b) it likely needs the same isInteractive-gate broadening proposed in donut-hover so a donut with only an AdvancedLabel (no popover) is still hoverable. requiresNewSignalOrScale: true - the swatch shape mark + 3-row text block is a wholly new mark type, not a reuse of an existing scale/signal (the connector-line path mark is now donut-advanced-labels-connector-line's concern). requiresS1S2Parity is false: there is no existing s1 AdvancedLabel implementation at all to mirror, so this is s2-only work by definition, not a parity gap.

implementationPlan.change: New file: AdvancedLabelOptions (labelKey?, value?: boolean, percent?: boolean, valueFormat?, percentFormat?, detail?: boolean) and AdvancedLabelSpecOptions (with defaults applied + donutOptions), following the SegmentLabelOptions/SegmentLabelSpecOptions pattern in segmentLabelSpec.types.ts.

New file: build the swatch mark (roundedSquarePath), the name/value/detail text marks (per-tier font sizes and colors above), and the hemisphere-mirrored block anchor offset (extending the direct-label technique to the whole block). Reuse the existing `_sumData`/aggregate total (from donutSummaryUtils.ts's getDonutSummaryData) for the detail row's 'out of {total}' value rather than adding a duplicate data source. Reuse donut-direct-labels-collision's donutLabelCollisionUtils.ts for collision avoidance (with this feature's ~58px minGap) rather than reimplementing it; the connector-line path mark is built separately in donut-advanced-labels-connector-line's util.
Add `advancedLabels?: AdvancedLabelOptions[]` to DonutOptions, following the existing `segmentLabels`/`donutSummaries` pattern.

Destructure `advancedLabels = []` in addDonut's produce callback, add it to the assembled donutOptions object, and call the new getAdvancedLabelMarks(options) in addMarks alongside getSegmentLabelMarks.
New file: AdvancedLabelProps extending AdvancedLabelOptions, following segmentLabel.types.ts's pattern.
New file: render-null component holding prop defaults, `displayName = 'AdvancedLabel'`, following SegmentLabel.tsx's pattern.
Add a `case AdvancedLabel.displayName:` to the shared children-to-options switch, collecting into an `advancedLabels` array, following the existing `segmentLabels`/`donutSummaries` cases.
implementationPlan.lines: N/A - new case in existing switch

implementationPlan.change: Destructure `advancedLabels` from `childrenToOptions(children)` and include it in the returned DonutOptions.

Add a test passing `createElement(AdvancedLabel)` as a child and asserting the resulting collection has length 1, following the existing segmentLabels/donutSummaries child tests (per this repo's childrenAdapter test-completeness convention).
New file: unit tests for the swatch/name/value/detail marks and the hemisphere anchor offset, following segmentLabelUtils.test.tsx's structure.

New file: stories covering the optional detail row, combining with direct labels, and hover-state color switching - following SegmentLabel.story.tsx's structure. (Connector-line-shape stories live in donut-advanced-labels-connector-line's story file.)

openQuestions: How is 'real text measurement' actually obtained at Vega-spec layout time, for both the block-width (ring-gap) and per-row-width (swatch-anchor-offset) calculations? Same unresolved question raised in donut-direct-labels - now applies to a 4-part block instead of 2 text lines.

Should this feature (and donut-hover's proposed isInteractive-gate broadening) extend to AdvancedLabel as well, so a donut with only an AdvancedLabel and no popover is still hoverable? Confirm scope overlap with the donut-hover spec rather than duplicating that decision independently.
Confirm whether advanced labels should be restricted for isBoolean donuts, consistent with the existing restriction on direct labels (SegmentLabel).

Confirm the two 'derived' (computed, not individually measured) values at each end of each typography row's tier range (name/value/detail at XS and XL) - donut-chart-tokens explicitly flags these as needing confirmation in Figma.
